subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What should the canonical inbound-media isolation boundary be across OpenClaw agents and channels: account-scoped, agent/session-scoped, tenant-aware, explicit-share based, or some combination?
rationale: The current report is a real privacy boundary gap, but the durable contract affects storage layout, plugin SDK media calls, sandbox paths, access checks, cleanup, and compatibility, so automation should not choose the security model alone.

options.title: Define Scoped Contract First
options.body: Choose the isolation unit, compatibility behavior, and explicit-sharing semantics before implementation touches shared media storage and staging paths.

options.title: Limit To Account Scoping
options.body: Implement the lower-friction account-based directory model and accept follow-up work for non-1:1 account-to-agent, tenant, and sharing cases.

options.title: Track Narrow Channel Slices Only
options.body: Leave this broad issue open but defer core changes until a maintainer sponsors the cross-channel managed-media design.

recommendation.title: Define Scoped Contract First
recommendation.body: Choose the isolation unit, compatibility behavior, and explicit-sharing semantics before implementation touches shared media storage and staging paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the clearest current history on the media store/reference path and already reviewed this issue as the broad tracker.
